query_text: I'm trying to get better at speaking English because there's a job opening at my company that deals with overseas clients and I really want it, but every time I open my mouth I just freeze up and my pronunciation is all over the place. I commute about 40 minutes each way so I was thinking — can you build me something I can use on my phone during that time, like a screen where I can hear a sentence and then record myself saying it back, and it tells me where I messed up? Like maybe highlights the words or sounds I got wrong, not just a score but actually shows me what was off. Dark background would be great so it's easy on the eyes when I'm on the subway. And some kind of little tracker so I can see if I'm actually improving week by week, otherwise I'll just give up like I always do with these apps.

query_text:
ok so I've been trying to stick to a vocab routine for IELTS but honestly every app I've tried just feels so... flat and boring? like I'll open it for two minutes and already want to close it. I need something that actually makes me *want* to sit with it during lunch or between classes, you know that feeling when an app just looks so pretty you keep opening it for no reason — I want that.

so build me a vocabulary practice page, kind of like flashcard-style where I can go through words one by one. the whole vibe should be that soft blurry glass look — like the cards are floating on top of a gradient background you can kind of see through, with that frosted layer effect. I want the cards to feel like they have depth, not just flat white boxes. maybe a dreamy purple-blue gradient or something that feels calm but a little luxurious.

when I tap a card it should flip over to reveal the meaning — the flip animation should feel smooth and satisfying, not choppy. the front shows the word big and clean, and the back shows the definition, maybe an example sentence, and the pronunciation. please also show some kind of subtle indicator at the top for how many words I've done vs total, like a soft progress bar that doesn't feel clinical.

I also want two buttons after revealing the meaning — something like "got it" and "review again" — so I can sort the words I'm shaky on. the buttons should match the aesthetic, maybe like frosted pill-shaped buttons, not those ugly solid-color rectangles. everything should feel layered and a bit dreamy — the card shadow, the background blur, even small hover or tap animations matter. pre-fill it with 15–20 real IELTS-level words so it feels like a working demo right away

query_text:
ok so I'm taking like three online courses at the same time right now — UI design stuff — and I keep forgetting where I left off on each one, it's honestly so annoying. I want a page that shows all my courses at a glance, like a dashboard kind of thing, and each course card should have that little progress bar showing how far I've gotten — percentage or something visual, not just numbers — because I need to see at a quick glance which ones I'm almost done with and which ones I've barely touched. 

also super important: if I haven't opened a course in like a few days, I want some kind of reminder or badge on it, like a little "hey you forgot about me" indicator, because I genuinely just go days without touching certain courses and then totally lose track. there should also be a "continue" button or something on each card so I can just tap and jump back to exactly where I stopped, no digging around.

the whole thing should feel kind of bright and fun, not boring or corporate looking — I'm thinking like some color, maybe different colors per course card so they don't all blend together. the layout should be clean though, like not cluttered, I hate when stuff is everywhere. oh and maybe at the top show which course I should prioritize, like the one I'm most behind on or haven't touched longest — some kind of "pick this one today" suggestion area. 

if a course is fully completed show that clearly too, like a done state that looks visually satisfying. the whole thing just needs to feel like I open it and immediately know what to do next without thinking

query_text:
ok so I'm trying to make like a prototype for a kids Chinese character learning app, my son is 7 and every time I show him those existing apps he's like "mom this is so boring" because they're all pink pastel baby stuff and he just closes it immediately. I play games myself and I feel like that whole neon-on-dark-background style, kinda like when you open a game lobby at night and everything is glowing — THAT is what would actually get a kid's attention.

So I need you to build me a main learning screen for this app. The whole page should have a dark background, like deep dark blue or black, and then the main thing in the center is a big character card showing one Chinese character — make it glow, like that neon light effect, the character itself should pulse or shimmer a little so it feels alive. Under the character show the pinyin with like a soft highlight. Then there should be a button or icon somewhere on the card that says something like "see how to write it" — this is the entry point to the stroke order animation, I don't need the animation itself built right now, just the button that would lead to it.

Around the card I want like floating sparkle particles or light streaks drifting in the background, nothing too crazy but enough that it doesn't look like a textbook. Also add some kind of progress indicator — maybe stars or XP points style, show like "3/10 characters today" but make it look like a game quest tracker not a homework checklist. 

At the bottom I want navigation for at least: Home, Learn, and a Rewards section (just tabs, no need to build those other pages). Use bright accent colors — electric blue, hot pink, maybe some lime green highlights — but keep the base dark. The font for the character should be big and bold, and the pinyin font should feel techy, not cute-roundy. I want to show this to some investors next month so it needs to look polished enough that they get the vibe immediately.

query_text:
I need a meeting notes app built out — dark background, please, because I'm constantly projecting in dim conference rooms and the bright white tools are basically unusable. The whole thing needs to feel fast and structured, not like a blank doc.

Here's what I need it to actually do: there's a left sidebar listing all my meetings (grouped by date, with the most recent on top), and when I click into one I get the main editor area. Inside a meeting, I can quickly add three types of items — a regular note/talking point, an action item, or a decision. Action items are the most important thing here. Each one needs a field for the task description, an assignee name (just text is fine, no need for accounts), and a due date picker. Those three fields should be visually distinct — like the assignee and due date should almost pop off the screen, bold or colored or something, because right now after every meeting I have to go back and re-read everything to figure out who said they'd do what.

At the top of every meeting view there should be a summary panel — like a quick-glance block that automatically lists just the action items in a table: task / owner / due date. That's literally the thing everyone argues about after the meeting, so it needs to be impossible to miss.

Also need a toolbar with basic formatting (bold, bullet list is enough), and a way to add attendee names at the start of a meeting. 

The export/share button should be prominent — when I click it, it generates a clean summary I can copy or download, showing the meeting title, date, attendees, key notes, and the action item table. The whole color palette should be dark gray/charcoal base with maybe a teal or amber accent for the action items so they stand out — not neon, just clearly readable from six feet away on a screen.

query_text:
okay so I've been thrown into this cross-team project and honestly the document situation is a complete mess — stuff is buried in old email threads, people have files sitting in their personal folders, and every time a new person joins they have zero idea where anything is or what decisions were already made. I need help building an internal doc hub page, kind of like a team wiki but more... alive? like you can actually see what's been touched recently and who did what.

Here's roughly what I'm picturing:

Left sidebar for organizing things into categories — product specs, meeting notes, decisions, onboarding stuff, whatever. Main area shows the docs. At the very top, a search bar that actually searches *inside* document content, not just titles, because people are going to need to dig up stuff from like six months ago.

Somewhere prominent — maybe a panel on the right or a strip near the top — there should be a recent activity feed. Something like "Zhang Wei updated the Q2 roadmap · 2h ago" or "New doc added: kickoff notes." Just a running log so people don't have to chase each other asking what changed.

Each doc should show as a card with the title, who last edited it, when, and maybe a tiny content preview. Clicking opens a clean reading view. I'd also love some kind of version indicator — even just showing "edited 3 times" or a small "last major update" timestamp — so people know whether they're looking at something stale.

And for new teammates specifically, I want a pinned "start here" section at the top of the main area — featured docs, key links, maybe a short welcome blurb. Something that helps them get oriented without bugging everyone.

Visual style — I want it to feel soft and calm, like the cards and panels are gently lifted off the background, that kind of tactile look with soft shadows and rounded edges. Muted tones, nothing harsh or too flat. The whole thing should feel like a place people actually want to spend time in, not a stressful tool. Responsive too, people will be using this on laptops during meetings.

okay so I need help building like a full weekly status report page, and I want it to actually look *designed*, not like something I threw together in Word on a Friday afternoon. my director basically told me our reports look too casual and I kind of want to prove him wrong next week lol

I manage three separate sub-projects so there should be some way to show each one separately but they all sit on the same page, like maybe each project gets its own little section or card thing

the layout — I want the left side to feel more like a summary/progress area and the right side to show numbers or status, but like... nicer than a plain table. also super important — when I screenshot it or print it to PDF to send to the overseas team, it still needs to look good. no cut-off edges, no weird fonts. 

please make it a single page, use some placeholder content so I can see how it all looks filled in, and make the overall feel polished — like something I'd actually be proud to send to a director

Ok so I'm going on this solo trip to Italy and France next month — 15 days total — and I'm really stressed about money because I have no idea how fast euros disappear when you're actually there. I want like a travel budget app thing that can help me plan before I leave AND track while I'm going. Here's what I'm picturing:

Before the trip, I want to put in my total budget (mine is roughly 20,000 RMB) and then split it up by city — like Rome for 4 days, Florence for 3 days, Paris for 5 days or whatever — and see how much I can spend each day in each place. I need to see both the euro amount AND what that equals in RMB side by side because honestly I keep losing track of what 80 euros even means in real money.

Then while I'm actually traveling, every time I spend something — coffee, museum ticket, dinner — I want to quickly log it and instantly see two things: how much of my daily budget I've used up today, and how much total budget I have left for the whole trip. Like a running total that updates every time I add an expense. Can it also show me a little breakdown by category, like food vs. attractions vs. transport?

The design should feel kind of pretty and modern, like those glossy frosted-glass style apps — soft backgrounds, cards that look layered, not a plain spreadsheet look. And please make it work well on mobile since I'll be using my phone the whole trip. Pre-fill it with some example cities and sample daily budgets so I can see how it's supposed to work right away.

query_text:
ok so I'm trying to plan this Yunnan trip for Golden Week — my parents' 30th anniversary and honestly I have zero clue where to start, I've been saving xiaohongshu posts for weeks but they're all over the place and I can't turn any of it into an actual plan. I need like a full travel itinerary builder app, where you tell it how many days you have (like 5 or 6 days) and who you're traveling with — because I'm bringing my parents and they really can't do a ton of walking, so it should factor that in and skip anything too intense or far apart. 

The main thing I want is a day-by-day layout — Day 1 do this, Day 2 go here — with the specific spots listed out per day, rough time estimates for each place (like "Lijiang Old Town: about 2-3 hours"), and maybe a note if something is old-person friendly or not. Each attraction card should have a photo, a short description, maybe star rating or a few user comments underneath, opening hours, ticket price if there is one. 

I also really want the overall layout to feel bright and easy to read at a glance — warm colors, big clear cards, nothing too cramped or text-heavy. My mom is going to want to see this so it has to look nice enough that I can just screenshot the whole thing and send it to the family group chat without having to explain anything. Oh and if I could toggle between different trip lengths or switch the traveler type (solo / couple / family with elderly) that would be amazing, so I can compare a 5-day vs 6-day plan side by side maybe. The app should feel kind of like a travel magazine, vibrant and inviting, not like a spreadsheet.

query_text:
ok so I've been keeping restaurant notes in my phone's memo app for like two years and it's an absolute disaster, I can never find anything when I actually need it and I'm constantly losing my favorite late-night spots in a wall of text — so I need a proper restaurant-saving app, specifically the main home screen where all my saved places live

the whole point is the VIBE. I'm out here at midnight wandering through neon-lit alleys finding incredible little hole-in-the-wall spots and I want an app that actually feels like that world, not some bright-white food delivery thing. think dark background, deep dark navy or almost black, with glowing neon accent colors — hot pink, electric teal, maybe some amber streetlight yellow. like if a city at 2am became an app. every time I open it I want to feel like I'm pulling up my own secret underground food map

for the actual layout I want cards for each saved restaurant, each card should feel like a little polaroid or a neon sign almost — show the restaurant name in a bold glowy font, maybe a tag for what kind of food it is, and like a tiny badge or label I can customize (stuff like "go back immediately" or "save for special nights" or "bring friends"). cards should be browsable in a scrollable grid, not a plain list, grid feels more like flipping through a personal collection

I also want some kind of visual texture difference between places I've been to recently vs ones I saved ages ago and haven't revisited — maybe the older ones look slightly dimmer or faded, like a photo developing in reverse. hovering or tapping a card should give it this subtle glow-pulse animation, nothing bouncy or cute, more like a flickering neon sign

at the top I want a search bar that feels embedded in the dark UI, not a stark white box, and maybe a row of filter tags underneath — by food type, by neighborhood, by my own custom labels. the whole header area could have a faint animated background, like slow-moving city light bokeh or something, very subtle not distracting

also a floating add button somewhere, glowing, to save a new place — when I tap it the form that pops up should match the same dark aesthetic, not suddenly flip into some bright modal that kills the mood

no ratings, no stars, no review scores — I genuinely don't care, I just need my own notes and my own labels. keep it personal, keep it dark, keep it feeling like mine

query_text:
ok so I need help building a mobile food ordering/menu browsing UI and the single most important thing is dark theme — like actually dark, not "dark-ish gray that still blinds you at 1am" dark. I'm always ordering food late at night in a dim room and every app that hits me with a white background instantly goes in the trash.

The core of it is the menu page. Each dish gets a card — photo needs to be big enough that I can actually tell what I'm looking at, not some postage-stamp thumbnail. And right on the card face, without tapping into anything, I need to see: dish name, price, and any key tags like spice level (mild / medium / spicy) or portion size. Those tags should be colored pill badges with strong contrast against the dark card — something that's readable even with my screen at like 40% brightness, because I've genuinely ordered the wrong spice level before from a bad UI and it was a whole thing.

For layout, don't make it feel like a spreadsheet. Not too crammed. Maybe single column, or two columns if each card has enough breathing room — I just don't want to feel like I'm squinting. Prioritize clarity over fitting more items on screen.

The spec selection flow is where most apps mess up. When I tap to add a dish, I do NOT want three nested popups. Give me a smooth bottom sheet that slides up, shows spice/size options as big tappable buttons, and has a clear "Add to Cart" CTA. Whole interaction should be like two taps and done. Cart should always be visible — a floating bar or sticky footer showing item count and total, so I'm never lost.

When an item gets added, give me a small satisfying animation — like the cart icon count bumps up, or a quick scale pop on the card. Nothing flashy, just enough feedback so I know it worked.

Handle these states: loading skeletons (dark-styled, no white flash), sold-out items (grayed-out card, disabled button, maybe a small "sold out" label), and an empty cart vs. cart with items. Pre-fill around 10 demo dishes — mix of mains, sides, different spice levels and price ranges — so the whole thing looks lived-in from the start.

ok so I really need help building a delivery tracking screen for a food order app — the whole thing has been bugging me for months and I finally want to get it right. I work from home and I'm constantly in back-to-back calls, so when I order lunch I literally cannot keep checking my phone every two minutes wondering if the rider is still five blocks away or like, already downstairs. once I waited over an hour and the status just... never updated. it was the worst.

there's also a little progress strip at the top — order confirmed, being prepared, picked up, on the way, delivered — with each stage clearly highlighted when it's active, and the transition should feel gentle, like a soft pulse or a glow, not a jarring color swap.

most importantly I want smart notifications baked into the UI itself: when the rider is 5 minutes away, something on screen should visibly change — maybe the background shifts warmer, or the arrival time starts a gentle countdown animation, something that catches my eye even if I glance away from a Zoom call. there should also be a rider detail card — name, little avatar, a simple "arrived" button they can tap, and a one-tap call icon — styled to match the soft raised card look everywhere else.

mobile layout only, portrait mode, the whole thing should feel calm and reassuring not stressful, and please prefill some mock rider location data so I can actually see the map dot moving and test the "almost here" state

query_text:
I've been trying basically every sudoku app out there and they all make me cringe a little — tiny ads crammed between the grid, numbers in that awful bold font that feels like it's shouting at you, backgrounds that look like they were designed in 2009. I just want something that feels like flipping open a beautifully typeset magazine, you know? Like the kind of calm you get when you open a fresh issue of Kinfolk. Lots of breathing room. Nothing fighting for your attention.

So I'd love help building a sudoku app that actually looks and feels like that. Here's what I'm imagining:

The grid itself should feel almost editorial — thin, quiet lines, generous spacing between cells, numbers in a single elegant serif or a very restrained sans-serif, nothing heavier than regular weight. The selected cell could have a very soft warm tint, not a harsh blue highlight box. Related cells (same row/column/box) should get just the faintest background shift, barely noticeable, like a shadow.

For colors: off-white or warm ivory background, not stark white. Ink-dark text. Maybe a muted terracotta or dusty sage as the one accent color — used sparingly, only for things like the active cell or completed rows. No gradients. No drop shadows. No glossy buttons.

The number input — I don't want a big ugly numpad cluttering the screen. Maybe the numbers appear as a minimal floating row right below the selected cell, or a quiet row at the bottom with enough padding that it doesn't feel cramped. Pencil notes (draft numbers) should look visually distinct but still refined — smaller, lighter, maybe in a slightly different color.

Difficulty selection should feel like choosing an article to read, not picking a video game level. Just clean labels: Easy, Calm, Focused, Hard — or something with that editorial tone. No stars, no trophies, no badges anywhere on screen unless I specifically open a stats page that I can choose to ignore.

Timer should be optional and hidden by default — I don't want to feel like I'm being timed while I'm trying to relax. If I turn it on, it should sit somewhere very discreet, small text, top corner.

Mistake highlighting: I'd prefer it to be optional too. Sometimes I want the gentle nudge (wrong number turns a soft red), sometimes I want to figure it out myself without any visual interruption. Let me toggle that in a simple settings panel — not buried in a confusing menu, just something clean and accessible.

When I complete a puzzle, I want a moment of quiet satisfaction — not confetti or animations flying everywhere. Maybe just a simple line of text, centered on a clean screen: "Puzzle complete." with the time underneath if I had that on. That's it. Like the white space at the end of a magazine essay.

The whole layout should work well on mobile, portrait orientation. And please make the overall spacing feel generous — I'd rather elements have too much room than feel packed in.

Also I want a small section for little milestone badges — like if you hit 7 days you unlock one, 30 days another, stuff like that, displayed in a row even if most are locked/greyed out. The whole thing should feel clean and airy, not cluttered, mostly white background with one accent color, the kind of design that feels calm but motivating. It should work well on mobile since that's where my friends will use it. Oh and pre-fill it with some fake data so it doesn't look empty when you first open it.

I have like almost 6000 photos on my phone — kids' birthdays, school events, a couple family trips, just... everything from the past few years all jumbled together — and every time I try to sort through them I just give up because there's no way I'm doing it one by one. I really need an app that can just automatically go through all of them and group things for me, like by the kids' faces separately (I have two kids so I want to be able to tap on my older one and see just her photos, same for the younger one), and also by time so I can find stuff like "that beach trip last summer" or "Chinese New Year 2024" without scrolling forever.

Nothing fancy, just clean and easy. My mom is turning 65 this year and I keep thinking I want to make her something with photos of the grandkids but I never get around to it because I can't find the right photos fast enough.

For the overall look, please keep it soft and warm — pastel colors, rounded cards, nothing that looks too technical or cluttered. Big buttons, clear labels. The app should feel like it's doing the hard work quietly in the background and just showing me the nice results, not making me learn how to use it.

query_text:
ok so i've been editing my cooking videos on my phone for like a year now and honestly the apps i use are just so plain and boring looking, i really want something that feels more... premium? like you know that frosted glass kind of look where everything has this soft blurry see-through layer behind it, kind of like the aesthetic you see on some lifestyle creator pages — that dreamy, layered feel where the cards look like they're floating a little. i want to build a mobile video editing page with that whole vibe.

here's what i'm thinking it should have: at the top there's a video preview area, big enough to see the full look of whatever clip i'm working on, and it should update in real time when i apply a filter or effect so i can feel whether it looks right before committing. below or on the side there should be a row of style presets — like warm golden hour, cool moody tone, that soft hazy look — shown as little thumbnail cards with the frosted glass card style, not just plain buttons. when i tap one it should smoothly transition onto the preview, not just snap.

then i need a simple timeline at the bottom, just enough to trim the clip, not anything too complicated with layers and tracks, just drag the handles on both ends to cut. there should also be a section for adding text overlays — just basic ones with a few font style options and color pickers — and maybe sticker or emoji placement where i can drag them around on the video frame.

the whole color scheme should feel soft and glassy, like muted purples or warm creamy tones with blur effects on the background panels. every card or panel should have that translucent frosted look, a little shadow underneath, rounded corners everywhere. i want it to feel like something you'd actually enjoy opening, not just a boring tool. animations when switching tabs or applying effects should feel smooth and satisfying, not janky. and everything has to be touch-friendly because i'm only ever using this on my phone, so buttons need to be big enough to tap without zooming in.

query_text:
Okay so I've been switching between like four different news apps because none of them let me actually control what I see — they just keep pushing celebrity gossip at me when I'm trying to stay on top of indie game releases and design trends. I want to build a content preference settings page that doesn't feel like filling out a tax form.

Here's the vibe I'm going for: neon, dark background, kinda cyberpunk — think glowing pill tags, maybe some subtle grid lines or scanline texture in the background. Not flashy for no reason, but definitely not the flat grey settings pages everyone keeps shipping.

Functionally it needs to do a few things. First, a topics section where I can see all the categories I'm tracking — things like UI/UX, indie games, open source, tech industry news — displayed as glowing tag chips I can toggle on/off with a satisfying click animation. Active tags should glow (like neon cyan or violet), inactive ones should dim out. Second, a blocked content section — same chip UI but in a red/warning palette, where I can add keywords or topics I never want to see (e.g. celebrity drama, crypto hype). Third, a feed source panel where I can see which publishers or RSS feeds I've subscribed to, reorder them by drag, and toggle each one. 

There should also be a "content diet summary" — like a small visual breakdown, maybe a ring chart or horizontal bar, showing the rough split of what topics I'm currently tuned to. Updates live as I toggle tags. 

Interactions: toggling a tag should animate smoothly, not just flash. Adding a keyword to the blocked list should let me type inline directly in that section without opening a modal. Dragging sources to reorder should feel snappy. And the whole thing should work well on both desktop and a mid-size tablet layout — doesn't need to be a full mobile build but it shouldn't break below 768px.

Pre-fill it with some example topics and blocked keywords so it doesn't look empty on first load.

These numbers should feel big and readable, not buried in a table.

Middle section is for hot sectors — show maybe 8 to 10 sector tiles, each showing the sector name, today's average gain/loss percentage, and maybe a tiny spark-style bar so you can feel if it's accelerating or fading. The top 3 gaining sectors should visually stand out more than the rest, maybe a subtle glow or brighter text. If a sector is down more than 2%, maybe a muted red tint on that tile.

Bottom section is a scrollable ticker-style event feed — earnings announcements, policy news, major company filings, that kind of thing. Each entry needs a timestamp, a short headline, and a colored tag like "policy", "earnings", "macro". Important stuff — like central bank moves or index rebalancing — should be pinned to the top with a little highlight badge.

One more thing: the whole page should auto-refresh every 60 seconds without a full reload so the data stays live. And please pre-fill it with some realistic mock data so we can show the boss what it'll look like before we hook up a real data source.

query_text:
I want to build a wishlist page — but not a wishlist page, if that makes sense. More like a curated editorial spread, the kind of thing you'd see if a design magazine did a "things we're coveting this season" feature. Every item I save should feel like it has its own moment on the page, not just dumped into a grid like a shopping cart.

Here's what I'm picturing: each saved item gets a big beautiful card — product image takes up most of it, very minimal text underneath, just the brand name, the price, and maybe a short note I can write myself (like "saw this in that Copenhagen store, felt so right"). I want generous whitespace between cards, nothing cramped. There should be a way to organize items into named collections — like I could have one called "kitchen objects I keep thinking about" and another for "things to hint at for my birthday."

The overall color palette should be neutral, warm off-white background, thin serif fonts, nothing screaming at me. Items should have a subtle status tag I can toggle — like "still thinking," "ready to buy," or "gifted/got it" — so I can track where I am in my decision process without it looking ugly. When something goes on sale or the price drops, a small quiet indicator would be lovely, not a loud badge, just a gentle signal.

I also really care about how this looks when screenshotted. The layout should hold up well in a full-page screenshot — clean top, no clutter — because I literally send these to friends as gift reference. Maybe a way to toggle into a "share view" that hides the status tags and just shows the beautiful product cards in a clean arrangement, almost like a mood board. On mobile it should feel like scrolling through a very well-edited magazine, slow and intentional, not infinite-scroll chaos.

query_text:
I keep coming back from trade shows with like 40, 50 business cards stuffed in my jacket and after two weeks I have no idea who half these people are anymore. My boss is now pushing everyone to get all contacts into the CRM system so I really need something that makes this fast.

I want a business card scanner app — basically I take a photo of a card and it pulls out the name, job title, company, phone number, and email automatically and shows it in a clean list. The list should have a card for each person with all their info laid out neatly, and I should be able to tap into a contact to edit anything the scan got wrong because sometimes the text is a bit blurry.

A few things that are really important to me: first, the main screen should be dead simple — just a big camera/scan button front and center, nothing cluttered. Second, once the list builds up I want to be able to search by name or company. Third, there should be a way to export everything, even just copying to clipboard or downloading as a spreadsheet would be fine. Fourth, I want some kind of status tag on each card like "followed up" or "pending" so I know which ones I've already reached out to.

Also if I scan a card that looks like a duplicate — same phone number or email as someone already in the list — I'd love a little warning so I don't end up with two entries for the same person. The whole thing should look clean and modern, not busy, light background, easy to read at a glance. I'm going to be using this on my phone mostly.

query_text:
ok so I've been a freelance illustrator for a few years now and my income is all over the place — some months I make decent money, other months it's like... where did everything go. I just got my credit card bill and it was way higher than I thought and I genuinely have no idea what I spent it on, so I really need something to help me actually see where my money goes each month.

I want a personal expense tracker page, like a dashboard kind of thing, focused on showing me a summary of what I've spent this month broken down by category — food and dining, shopping, transport, subscriptions, that kind of stuff. I'm not looking for anything complicated, I just want to look at it and immediately understand "oh I blew too much on takeout again."

Here's what I'm thinking for the page: there should be a big clear number at the top showing my total spending this month, then below that show each spending category as like a card or a section with its own total — each one should have a little icon or color so I can tell them apart at a glance. Maybe a horizontal or donut chart somewhere that shows the proportion visually, because I'm more of a visual person. If a category is unusually high compared to the others it should stand out somehow, like a different color or a little tag.

There should also be a way to add a new expense entry — just a simple form, pick a category, enter an amount, add a short note and a date. Nothing more than that. When I add something it should update the totals on the page without me having to refresh. 

The whole thing should feel clean and not overwhelming — I've tried budget spreadsheets before and they just stressed me out. Use Material Design style, soft colors, smooth little animations when numbers update or when I add an entry. Should work fine on mobile since I'd mostly be checking it on my phone. Pre-fill it with some sample data so it doesn't look empty when I open it for the first time.

query_text:
okay so I've been juggling like five client projects at once and I keep missing follow-up dates because my current reminder app is just... so boring and flat, I literally scroll past it without registering anything. I want to build a reminder management page that actually *looks* urgent when something is urgent, you know? like the whole thing should have that frosted glass vibe — cards that feel layered, slightly see-through, with a soft blurry background behind them so it looks really pretty but also super organized.

The main thing I need is for all my reminders to be grouped by how urgent they are — like a "🔥 Today / Critical" section at the top that you literally cannot ignore, then a "This Week" middle section, and a softer "Upcoming" area below. Each card should show the task name, the time or deadline, a little colored tag (like I can label things as "Client Reply", "Submission", "Invoice", whatever), and some kind of priority badge or indicator — maybe a glowing dot or a bold stripe on the side.

The cards in the top urgent group should feel visually heavier, maybe a warmer tint or more intense glass effect, compared to the calmer cards further down. I want to open the page and in literally two seconds know what I absolutely have to deal with today. 

Also there should be a way to mark a reminder as done right from the card — like swipe or a little check button — and when something's marked done it fades out nicely, not just disappears. And at the top of the page a small summary line like "3 things need your attention today" would be so helpful. The whole layout should be mobile-first, with enough breathing room between cards so it doesn't feel cramped. Soft shadows, layered depth, colors that actually feel different per priority level — not just red/yellow/green but something more aesthetic than that

query_text:
ok so I need to build a step-by-step onboarding setup wizard for a new collaboration tool — basically what I WISH had existed when I joined my current company last week and had to set everything up alone with zero instructions, just an invite link in an email and absolutely nothing else to go on lol

the whole flow should be like 4 or 5 steps total. first a welcome screen right after the user clicks their invite link, then a step to fill in basic profile info (name, role, maybe a profile photo), then some workspace or notification preferences, then a team setup step where you can accept a pending team invite or send invites to other people, and finally a "you're all done!" screen that makes it really obvious the setup is actually complete and you're good to go

every step needs to feel super clear — I want a progress bar at the top showing like "step 2 of 5" so nobody feels lost, and the Next button should only activate when the required fields are filled in, not just let you click through with empty stuff. if something is missing, highlight that field gently with a little message, don't just do nothing. also a Back button that actually keeps whatever I already typed — if I go back to fix something I shouldn't have to retype the whole thing

the final confirmation screen is really the most important part to me — I want it to show a summary of everything that got configured (profile, team, settings), with a visible checkmark animation or something that feels like it's celebrating, like yes you actually finished!! and if there were optional steps skipped, show those as soft "you can do this later" suggestions, not errors, so it doesn't feel like I failed

design should be colorful and lively, high saturation, round corners, friendly vibes — definitely not corporate gray. also needs to be responsive and work on mobile since a lot of people will probably click invite links from their phones

query_text:
I want to build a research dashboard — think Bloomberg Terminal meets Nansen meets something out of a cyberpunk anime, dark background, neon accent colors (electric cyan, acid green, maybe some deep purple), the kind of thing that makes someone who opens it go "okay this person is serious." This is my main analysis workbench for onchain data but I also want it to serve as a showcase page for potential subscribers so it needs to look absolutely ruthless at first glance.

Layout: a dense multi-panel grid. I'm thinking a top status bar with live-ish metric chips — TVL, protocol revenue, active wallets 24h, gas, ETH dominance — just numbers with small delta indicators, color-coded green/red. Below that, the main area splits into a large chart panel on the left (takes up maybe 60% width) and a right column with stacked smaller cards. The big chart should support multiple overlapping line series with a legend, and I want the ability to toggle between different timeframes (1D / 7D / 30D / 90D) with smooth transitions. The right column has: a protocol health scorecard with bar-style indicators, a "whale wallet tracker" table showing recent large movements (address, amount, direction, timestamp), and a competitive landscape mini-heatmap comparing 4-5 protocols across key metrics.

At the bottom, a full-width section — "Research Feed" — showing a list of recent insight cards, each with a tag (e.g. "Liquidity Risk", "Token Unlock", "Governance"), a one-line summary, and a severity badge. These cards should have a subtle hover glow effect consistent with the neon theme.

Animation-wise: on load, panels should fade/slide in staggered, numbers should count up from zero. Hovering chart data points shows a tooltip with full detail. The whole thing should feel alive even with static/mock data baked in — pre-populate everything so it doesn't look empty. Sidebar nav on the left edge, minimal, icon-only with tooltips.

Use dark charcoal or near-black (#0d0f14 range) as the base, neon cyan as primary accent, keep font monospace or semi-monospace for all data values to reinforce the terminal aesthetic. Make it responsive enough to not break on 1440p wide monitors.

query_text:
Okay so I'm rebuilding our studio's website from scratch and I really need help putting together the main showcase page — the one that does all the heavy lifting before anyone even scrolls. The whole vibe I'm going for is... like if you walked into a gallery at night, everything quiet and dark, and the work just *glows* at you. That feeling. So the background needs to be deep, almost charcoal or near-black, not just grey, and the typography should feel editorial — clean but with some weight to it, like a high-end print magazine.

Here's roughly what I'm thinking for the layout:

**Hero section** — full viewport, dark background, studio name centered or slightly left-aligned, maybe a short punchy line underneath (like a one-liner about what we do — sustainable materials, thoughtful design). Behind or beside the text there should be one large textured or moody image, could be a project photo. I want a subtle animation on load, nothing crazy, just like the text fading up or a slow reveal, the kind that feels intentional not gimmicky.

**Work/Projects section** — a grid of our best pieces, maybe 3 columns, with project title and a category tag on hover. Each card should have a dark overlay that lifts slightly when you hover so the image breathes a little. No carousels please, I hate carousels.

**About/Team section** — keep it minimal, a short paragraph about the studio's philosophy on one side, and on the other side maybe 3–4 team member photos in a clean row, names + role underneath. The tone should feel human but not casual — think "craft meets intention."

**Contact section** — at the bottom, just an email address that's large and clickable, maybe a subtle "let's talk" above it, and links to Instagram and LinkedIn as icons. No contact form, too much friction.

Overall the page should scroll smoothly, all sections connected, no jarring jumps. On mobile everything should stack gracefully — the grid goes to 1 column, text scales down but stays legible. Accent color should be something warm — like a muted gold or warm off-white — used sparingly just for highlights or hover states, never loud. I want someone landing on this page to immediately feel like we know what we're doing without us having to say it.

query_text:
ok so I'm trying to plan a 5-day trip to Kyoto and Osaka for me and my parents and I have like 30+ notes saved from travel blogs but I genuinely have no idea how to turn all of that into an actual schedule that makes sense day by day. My parents have never been abroad before and my mom's knees aren't the best so I really can't just pile everything into one day and hope for the best — I need to actually see if the pacing is reasonable before we leave.

What I'm imagining is some kind of visual planner where I can take all the spots I've already picked and slot them into morning / afternoon / evening blocks for each day, and then it automatically estimates the travel time between each stop so I don't have to manually look up every single transit route. Each attraction card should probably show rough visit duration, estimated cost, and maybe like a small note if the place involves a lot of stairs or walking — just so I can keep an eye on that for my parents.

I also want a budget summary somewhere — broken down by category like transport, meals, entrance fees, that kind of thing — with a running total that updates as I add or remove things. I have a number in my head but I'm honestly not sure if it covers everything once you add it all up.

For the look, I'd love that frosted glass card style — like each day is its own layered glass panel floating over a soft blurred background, maybe with warm sakura-y tones or something that feels a little Japanese but still clean and modern. Every planner I've tried so far looks like a spreadsheet and it just makes me more anxious, so I really want something that feels calm and easy to scan at a glance.

query_text:
okay so I keep forgetting stuff every time I travel for work — last trip I showed up without a power adapter, the time before that I left my portable charger at home — and I'm so done relying on memory. I want to build a packing checklist app, kind of like a pre-flight mental checklist but actually useful. Here's what I'm imagining:

When I open it, I should be able to pick a trip type first — like "domestic short trip", "international 3-5 days", "Southeast Asia business trip" etc. — and based on that it pulls up a pre-loaded checklist of items I'd typically need. Not just a flat list either, I want items grouped into categories like Documents, Electronics, Toiletries, Clothes, Misc — with little section headers so it's easy to scan.

Each item should have a checkbox I can tap to mark done. I want to be able to add my own custom items too, and delete ones I never need. Most importantly, once I check something off, it remembers it — so next time I start a similar trip type, it pre-fills my customized version, not just the default template.

On the main screen I want to see something like "8 of 23 items packed" with a progress bar — the kind of satisfying visual feedback like you get on a progress tracker. If I leave items unchecked and it's close to my trip date... actually ignore the date stuff, that's too complicated. Just the checklist and templates.

Design should feel clean and minimal — lots of whitespace, not cluttered like a notes app. Mobile-first layout, simple color scheme, nothing flashy.

query_text:
ok so I drive like crazy hours for work — we're talking leaving at 5am or getting home past midnight pretty much every week, hitting hospitals across multiple cities. and the thing that kills me is when I glance at my navigation app and the screen is just... blasting light into my eyes on a dark highway. I nearly drifted once trying to figure out where my turn was. so I switched to this dark-theme routing app but honestly the layout still isn't great for a quick eyes-up glance while driving.

what I need is basically a redesigned main navigation screen — dark background obviously, but the stuff that matters has to POP. like the current road I'm on should be super visible, big enough to read without squinting. the upcoming turn direction — that arrow or whatever — needs to be impossible to miss, like highlight it differently from everything else on screen, maybe brighter or bigger or both. and the ETA, I always want that somewhere my eyes naturally land without hunting for it.

everything else — the map details, street labels, secondary info — should stay dim and out of the way so it doesn't compete. the whole point is I look over for one second and I already know: what road I'm on, where I'm turning next, how long till I arrive. done.

also think about the layout hierarchy — like if I'm driving and can only process three things, those three things are the ones I listed. maybe the turn indicator takes up a solid chunk of the top, current road name just below it or beside it, and ETA tucked in a corner but still readable. I don't want a cluttered panel with a bunch of icons and numbers all the same size and brightness, that's exactly what I'm trying to get away from.

bonus if there's a subtle visual difference when a turn is coming up really soon vs still several minutes away — like some kind of state change so I know when to actually pay attention vs when I can chill. not asking for animations that are distracting, just something clear enough that even in my peripheral vision I can tell things are changing.

query_text:
ok so I need a weather app but not like a regular weather app — I bike to work every single day, about 25 minutes each way, and I keep getting caught in rain halfway there which is the worst. so I basically need something that opens up and immediately tells me "you're fine, go" or "bring a raincoat" without me having to dig through numbers and charts

the main screen should show me right now + the next 2 hours, that's really all I care about before I leave the house. I want a big clear rain risk indicator — not just a percentage I have to interpret, more like a simple visual that goes from green to yellow to red depending on how likely it is to rain during my ride window. if there's rain coming, show me roughly when it starts, like "light rain around 8:40am" kind of thing

also I really want feels-like temperature front and center, not just the actual temp. sometimes it says 18°C and I walk out and it's freezing because of wind or whatever. so show me what it actually feels like and maybe a quick suggestion like "light jacket" or "just a t-shirt" — I don't need a full outfit breakdown, just a one-liner

the layout should be super clean, nothing cluttered, I'm usually half awake when I check this. big text, strong visual contrast. use Material design, clear color coding for the different risk levels. if the rain risk jumps from low to high within my commute window, highlight that change somehow — like a little warning banner or a color shift on the timeline

also a small hourly strip showing the next 6 hours would be nice below the main card, with tiny rain icons and feels-like temp per hour. keep it scrollable but compact. no ads, no news, no "top weather stories", just the stuff that helps me decide whether to get on my bike or take the subway

oh and animations — when the weather status changes, like if it updates and rain is now more likely, have a subtle transition so I notice something changed rather than just silently swapping numbers

pre-fill it with Beijing weather data so it feels real when demoing

query_text:
ok so I'm trying to build like a train/high-speed rail ticket search page for my school project and also honestly I just want something like this for myself lol — every holiday I'm scrambling to figure out which train home is cheapest and I never know if leaving at 6am vs noon actually saves me that much money

so here's what I'm thinking: the main screen should let me pick my departure city and destination, and then show me ALL the available trains for that day in like a scrollable list — sorted by departure time by default but I also wanna be able to sort by price. Each row in the list should show the train number, departure time, arrival time, travel duration, and then the prices for different seat types side by side (like second class, first class, business) so I can compare at a glance without tapping into each one separately

the tricky part is I also want some kind of visual thing — maybe a bar chart or a color-coded heatmap by hour — that shows which departure windows are generally cheaper, like a "price trend by time of day" strip above the list so I can immediately see that 7am trains cost way less than 5pm ones

also if a direct train is too expensive, I want the page to suggest a transfer option — like show me "via City X, total ¥89" as an alternative card below the direct results, with the transfer time and layover duration clearly labeled. the cheapest overall option should be highlighted somehow, maybe a little badge or a bright accent color since the whole thing should feel lively and colorful, not boring gray

when I tap any train row it should expand to show seat availability (how many seats left) and maybe a small "book now" button that links out to the actual ticketing platform. the whole thing needs to work well on mobile since I'm always doing this on my phone while rushing around campus

query_text:
okay so me and my coworkers literally spend half our lunch break just arguing about what to eat and we still end up at the same noodle place every single time lmao, so I want to build this little app that just... makes the decision for us. like you open it and there's basically one big button that says something like "decide for me" and it just spits out a random nearby restaurant, done, no more group chat chaos.

but I do want some light filtering before the random spin happens — like just big flavor categories, think spicy, light/healthy, rice dishes, noodles, fast food, that kind of thing, maybe 6-8 options max shown as big tappable pills or chunky icons so it's fast to pick. you don't have to pick one if you really don't care, just hit the button and go full random. after you tap, I want some kind of fun animation — like a spinning wheel or a slot machine thing, something that feels satisfying, not just a boring page reload — and then it lands on one result: restaurant name, rough distance or walk time, cuisine type, maybe a vibe tag like "cozy" or "quick bite," and one big call-to-action button to open maps.

also there should be a "nope, pick again" button on the result card so if you get something you really don't want you can reroll once or twice without going all the way back. the whole color scheme should feel energetic and fun — like warm oranges, yellows, maybe a pop of red, not some cold minimalist thing, I don't want it looking like a productivity tool. keep the layout super clean though, big text, lots of breathing room, definitely mobile first because nobody's pulling out a laptop at noon. pre-fill it with like 10-15 fake restaurant entries so it actually works and looks alive when you first open it

I need a smart kitchen app — basically I open my fridge on weekends and there's always random stuff in there, like half a block of tofu, some eggs, a carrot, maybe leftover pork from last night, whatever. I need something where I can just type in those ingredients real quick and it shows me one or two recipes I can actually make without running to the store. The input part should be super simple — like just a text box or maybe little ingredient tags I can add one by one, nothing complicated. Then when it shows the recipe, the steps need to be clear and short, written like a normal person would explain it, not like a cooking textbook. Maybe numbered steps with short sentences. If there's a timing note like "stir for 2 minutes" or "cook on medium heat" that's really helpful.

Also really want to see a rough portion guide — like "serves 3-4 people" — and maybe some basic nutrition info, nothing medical just like is it high protein or mostly carbs, that kind of thing. Keep the design clean and uncluttered, big text, easy to read while I'm standing at the stove. I don't want a million buttons or tabs everywhere. If a recipe has a photo that would be great but not required. Should work fine on mobile since I'm always on my phone in the kitchen.

query_text:
ok so I'm trying to build this restaurant discovery app and I need it to feel really premium, like when you open it you immediately think "wow this looks expensive" — you know that frosted glass kind of look where you can kind of see stuff blurred behind the cards? I want that. Every restaurant should show up as a card and the card needs to have a big beautiful photo at the top, the restaurant name, a star rating (like clearly visible, big enough that I don't have to squint), a short vibe tag like "cozy brunch spot" or "great for groups", and maybe distance from me.

The main screen should be a scrollable list of nearby places and I want some filter pills at the top — stuff like cuisine type, rating above 4.5, distance within 2km, that kind of thing. Tapping a pill should instantly filter the list without reloading the whole page, feels way smoother that way.

When I tap a restaurant card it should expand or go to a detail page with a photo gallery at the top (swipeable, like stories), then the rating breakdown, and then real user reviews with photos attached — the photos should be in a little horizontal scroll row so I can flick through them quickly. If a restaurant has a lot of 5-star photo reviews it should feel like that's front and center because honestly that's how I decide if a place is worth going.

Also the background of the whole app should have this soft gradient — maybe deep purple to midnight blue — so the frosted glass cards really pop against it. Subtle card shadows, smooth animations when cards load in, and when I tap something it should feel responsive, a little press effect or scale animation. No clunky transitions. The whole thing should feel like something I'd want to screenshot and show my friends, not just a plain list of restaurants.

ok so I need a spinning wheel page for my club parties — like those colorful fortune wheel things you see at events, but way more flashy and fun because we're gonna project it on a big screen in front of everyone so it HAS to look amazing. Oh and the overall vibe should be party-mode — loud colors, fun fonts, the kind of thing that makes a room go "ooooh" when it lands. query_text:
ok so I need help building a leaderboard and score page for a mini-game app, the kind of thing you'd open while waiting for the subway. basically I want to see my rank and my total score the second the page loads — like big and obvious right at the top, not hidden somewhere I have to hunt for it. I found out I'm like top 5 in one of my games and I wanna show my friends but there's nowhere to actually like... see it properly or share it.

the look is really important to me — I want that soft raised kind of style, like everything is slightly floating up from the background, buttons have that little shadow on both sides, background feels warm and creamy not just flat white. like a biscuit or foam texture almost, I know that sounds weird but you know the type. warm off-white base, maybe some soft pastel accents, nothing too bright or sharp on the eyes.

for the page itself: my avatar and username at the top, then a big card with my score and rank — and if I'm top 3 make it feel special, like a golden glow or a little crown badge or something. then below that a friends list showing each person's rank, score, and how far ahead or behind me they are. I want a little challenge or invite button next to each friend. if someone hasn't played recently their card should look kind of faded or greyed out so I know they're inactive. 

also a share button that lets me screenshot or copy my ranking to flex to my groupchat. and when scores update the list should animate smoothly — like cards sliding into new positions, nothing janky. the whole thing should feel like part of the game experience not just a boring scoreboard table. pre-fill some fake friend data so it doesn't look empty

query_text:
okay so I really need help building something and I don't even know exactly how to describe it but I'll try — basically I get home after like 10+ hours of work and my brain just won't shut off, and I keep picking up my phone trying to find something to just... exist in for a few minutes without having to think. most apps I try are way too loud and bright and they want me to set goals or read instructions and honestly that makes things worse.

what I want is something that opens up and immediately — like within a few seconds — just puts me in this quiet dark space. no loading tips, no "welcome" screens, no tutorial overlays, nothing. just a dark background, maybe deep navy or almost-black, and some things I can poke at. like little glowy shapes or blobs or particles or whatever, and when I tap one or drag it around it does something satisfying — maybe it ripples, maybe it stretches and snaps back, maybe it slowly floats away and fades. that kind of thing. the feedback has to feel immediate, like the thing actually reacts to my finger right away, not half a second later.

I want a few different interactive "objects" or zones on screen — not too many, maybe 3 to 5 — each with a slightly different behavior. one could be like a soft glowing circle you can press and hold and it slowly expands then gently contracts. another could be a cluster of small dots that scatter when you swipe through them and slowly drift back. something like that. the point is each thing feels different to touch but none of them are surprising or jarring.

no score. no timer. no achievement. no "you did great!" popup. nothing that tells me I did something right or wrong. no sound by default (or maybe the option to have a very quiet ambient hum, nothing percussive). the whole color palette should stay dark, low contrast overall except the interactive elements themselves should have this subtle glow so they're easy to spot without being harsh on the eyes.

and please don't put any navigation bars or menus or settings buttons cluttering the screen — if there has to be a settings option, make it like one tiny icon tucked in a corner that I'd only notice if I was looking for it. the main screen should just feel like... open space. quiet. mine to poke at if I want, or just look at if I don't.

query_text:
Okay so I need to build a card generator — specifically for producing really polished digital cards for boutique clients, think hotel seasonal greetings, new collection drop announcements, event invites, that kind of thing. The whole visual vibe has to feel very editorial and restrained, lots of breathing room, like something out of Monocle or Kinfolk, not cute or busy — just clean and considered.

Here's what I'm thinking for the actual tool:

A template library right on the landing screen — maybe 10–15 layouts sorted loosely by occasion (seasonal greeting, product launch, event invite, general announcement). Each template should already look finished and intentional out of the box, with good typographic hierarchy baked in, so even before I touch anything it reads as "designed." Mostly portrait format since these get shared over email and Instagram DM.

Once I pick a template I want to edit the text directly on the card — click the headline, type mine, done. No separate sidebar form. There should be a headline slot, a subline, and a small body block. For branding I just want to drop in one or two hex colors and have the template absorb them intelligently — like tinting an accent strip or the background wash, not randomly coloring everything. Don't make me pick specific fonts, just give me maybe three typographic mood options, something like classic serif / clean sans / editorial mixed, and apply it as a package.

A fullscreen preview mode with zero UI chrome so I can see exactly what the client sees before approving. Then export as a high-res PNG — at least 2× for retina — and ideally PDF too. The whole flow from opening the tool to having an export-ready file should feel achievable in under 15 minutes with no prior experience, so nothing buried in settings menus.

On mobile the preview should at least be readable since clients want to sign off quickly on their phones.

query_text:
I've got a media center PC hooked up to a projector in my living room and I need a proper UI for it — something that can handle a local library of like 400+ movies and concert videos. Think dark theme, deep blacks, the kind of thing that looks good when the room lights are completely off. Big poster art, big titles, I don't want to be squinting across the room trying to read tiny text.

Here's what I'm picturing: a full-screen home screen with a hero banner at the top — auto-rotating through recently added or "continue watching" stuff — and then below that a horizontal scrollable grid of movie posters organized by category (movies, concerts, TV series). Poster cards should show the title underneath in a clean bold font, maybe a subtle rating badge in the corner. When I hover/focus on a card it should scale up a bit and maybe show a quick-info overlay with year, duration, and genre tags. Nothing too busy.

The playback screen is the big one. I want a minimal overlay that fades out after a couple seconds — just a progress bar at the bottom, current timestamp, total duration, and the title up top. The progress bar should be thick enough to actually see from the couch. When I nudge it back into view (remote or keyboard), I need quick-access buttons for: skip back 10s, play/pause, skip forward 30s, and then on the right side of the bar — audio track selector and subtitle selector. These should pop up as a small panel (not a full modal), so my wife doesn't accidentally lose her place in a show trying to switch subtitles. Like Plex does it, kind of a slide-up tray. But cleaner.

Volume and brightness indicators should be these big translucent pill overlays that appear briefly when adjusted and then fade away — similar to how Kodi handles it but without the clunky UI. Also want a "back to library" button that doesn't nuke the playback state, so if she walks away and comes back she can resume without starting from scratch.

Color palette: near-black background (#0d0d0d or similar), accent color maybe a warm amber or electric blue for highlights and active states, white text for titles, gray for metadata. No gradients that look washed out on projectors. Keep icon sizes generous — minimum 28px, probably bigger for the player controls.

query_text:
So I spend like 40 minutes on the subway twice a day just scrolling through news, but my sources are all over the place — tech blogs, industry newsletters, business sites — and I'm constantly switching between apps which is exhausting. I really want to build a content aggregator feed that pulls everything into one clean card-based stream.

Here's how I picture it working: each card should show the headline, source name, maybe a thumbnail if there is one, and the publish time — nothing more, I don't need walls of text on the card itself. The cards stack in an infinite scroll, smooth enough that it doesn't stutter when I'm on a moving train. I want to be able to swipe or tap quickly to mark something as read so it fades out or gets visually dimmed, and there should be a separate bookmark action — like a little icon I tap if I want to read the full thing later when I'm at my desk. The bookmarked stuff goes into its own saved list somewhere accessible.

At the top I'd love filter pills or tabs — like "Tech", "Business", "Ecommerce", "All" — so I can narrow the feed by category depending on my mood. When I mark something read it should feel responsive, a quick animation or color change, not just silently disappear. The overall look should stay clean and not visual overload — Material style but minimal, lots of white space, clear typography hierarchy so my eyes can scan fast. 

Also a bottom nav: Feed, Saved, and maybe a Settings or Sources tab where I can toggle which feeds show up. The saved/read states should persist so when I reopen the app it remembers what I've already gone through. Pre-fill it with some demo articles across a few categories so it looks real from the start.

query_text:
I spend like an hour on the subway every day and I really want something that actually lets me sit and read a full article without my eyes hurting halfway through. Right now most news apps I use — the text is too small, the background is too bright, and there's always some banner or pop-up pushing ads in the middle of the article and I just give up. So I need a clean article reading page, something where when you open a story it just feels calm and easy on the eyes.

Here's what matters to me: first the text has to be big enough to read one-handed on a phone without squinting, and I need to be able to bump the font size up or down myself. Second, there should be a dark mode — not just "slightly grey" but a proper dark background with soft white text, because I'm usually in the subway or in a dim room during lunch and the bright white screen kills me after five minutes. The switch between light and dark should be easy to find, like right there on the reading screen, not buried somewhere in settings.

The layout itself — please make it breathable. Wide margins, decent line spacing, no cluttered sidebars or related-article carousels popping in while I'm reading. Just the headline, maybe a cover image, then the text. Progress bar at the top so I know how far along I am in a long piece would be nice.

At the bottom or somewhere obvious, I need a save button and a share button. When I find something good I want to forward it to a colleague on WeChat in like two taps, not hunt around for a hidden menu. The share should just copy a link or open the system share sheet. Save just bookmarks it locally, no account needed.

Oh and if the article is really long, a floating "back to top" button would help. Mobile first, the whole thing is really just for phone use.

query_text:
I need a proper RSS feed manager UI — dark theme, high contrast, the whole thing. Right now my subscription list is just one giant pile and I've literally missed important AI paper drops because they got buried under a bunch of low-signal noise sources that update fifty times a day.

What I want is a sidebar or panel that shows all my subscriptions organized into groups — but not just manually labeled folders. I want the app to visually distinguish between sources that update frequently (like multiple times a day) versus ones that only post once a week or less, maybe with a subtle tag or badge so I can scan at a glance. Let me drag feeds between custom groups too, like "Daily Scan", "Deep Read", "Finance", "Open Source" — that kind of thing.

For each feed in the list, I need to see: unread count (bold, high contrast so it jumps out), the last time something new was published, and some kind of staleness indicator — like if a source hasn't posted anything in 30+ days, flag it differently so I know to maybe drop it. Think of it like an inbox where dead sources are grayed out or marked as "gone quiet."

The overall layout should feel like a command center — dark background, maybe near-black with slightly lighter cards, accent colors only where something actually needs my attention. Unread counts in a bright color, stale feeds in muted gray. Let me also collapse/expand groups so I can hide the stuff I've already caught up on. A quick "mark all as read" per group would help a lot too.

query_text:
Build me a portfolio dashboard page — I've got holdings spread across like 4-5 different platforms (brokerage, crypto wallet, a couple fund apps) and every time I want to know how I'm actually doing overall I have to log into each one separately and do the math in my head, which is a nightmare. I want one single page that aggregates everything visually so I can tell at a glance what's going on.

Here's what I need it to do:

**Top section** — a summary bar or hero area showing total asset value across all accounts, today's overall gain/loss (amount + percentage), and a quick comparison to last month's total. Like a "you're up X% vs last month" kind of callout. Make it feel satisfying to look at.

**Account breakdown** — show each platform/account as its own card. Each card should have the account name, current value, today's change, and maybe a small sparkline or mini chart for recent trend. I want to be able to collapse or expand them.

**Asset allocation** — a donut or pie chart that shows how my total money is split across categories: stocks, crypto, funds, cash etc. Hovering or tapping a slice should highlight that portion and show the exact amount + percentage.

**Holdings list** — a sortable table or list of individual positions across all accounts. Columns: asset name, account it's in, current price, quantity, current value, gain/loss (both $ and %). I should be able to sort by any column and filter by account or asset type.

**Month-over-month comparison** — some kind of bar or line chart showing total portfolio value at end of each month for the last 6-12 months, so I can actually see if I'm trending up or down.

Design should use a glassmorphism style — frosted glass cards, subtle backdrop blur, layered depth effect, dark or deep background with light translucent card surfaces. Should look clean and modern, not like some old finance tool. Use some accent colors for positive/negative values (green/red) but keep the overall palette cohesive, not garish.

Pre-fill it with realistic mock data — a few accounts, maybe 10-15 positions across stocks, ETFs, and crypto — so it actually looks like a real dashboard when I open it. Everything should be interactive: sortable tables, hoverable charts, maybe a toggle between today's view and monthly view.

Ok so I really need help building a home budget tracking app, like a proper one, because right now I'm just using my phone notes app and every month-end I'm like wait where did all the money go?? What I really want is like a main summary page that shows me at a glance how much we've spent this month in each category — like a pie chart or those colored bar things, and it should be super obvious which categories have already gone over budget, maybe highlight them in red or something. Also I need to be able to set a monthly budget for each category, so the app can tell me like "hey you've used 90% of your grocery budget already." A little warning or badge would be helpful.

And this is really important — my husband travels for work all the time so he never sees what I'm spending, and he always asks me at the end of the month. So I need the account to be shareable so he can log in on his phone and see everything I've entered, in real time. He doesn't need to add stuff, just view. But I'd feel better if there was some kind of simple login.

Please follow Material Design style — clear buttons, obvious feedback when I tap things. And make it work well on mobile since that's all I'll ever use.

query_text:
ok so I'm a freelance illustrator and this year is literally my first time filing taxes on my own and I'm lowkey panicking. my income comes from like three or four totally different places — design platforms, clients who hire me directly, and occasionally someone pays me a licensing fee to use my artwork, which is never the same amount twice. everything is scattered all over the place and I have zero idea how much I actually owe.

so I need a page where I can log all my income entries one by one — each one should have a label for where the money came from, the amount, and maybe roughly when I got it — and then the page automatically adds it all up and gives me a ballpark estimate of how much tax I probably need to pay. I genuinely don't understand tax brackets or what I can deduct so if the calculation can be shown in plain simple steps somewhere that'd be really helpful, like just walk me through where the final number came from without assuming I know anything.

also I'm really stressed about missing the filing deadline so there needs to be something at the top of the page showing exactly how many days I have left — like a countdown, something I can't miss. if it's getting close maybe it changes color or something to get my attention.

the whole thing needs to feel really clean and not overwhelming — I shut down when a page has too much stuff on it. maybe income list on one side, tax estimate on the other, and the deadline warning pinned up top. I want to open it and immediately know my situation without reading paragraphs. and it has to work on mobile because I'm almost never at my desk when I need this stuff

query_text:
I've been having these random dizzy spells and my heart just like... races out of nowhere, especially at night after work, been going on for maybe two weeks now. I really want to go see a doctor but honestly booking an appointment is such a hassle and I'm not even sure if it's serious enough to take a day off for — so I want to build a symptom self-check tool that helps people like me figure out how urgent their situation actually is.

Here's what I'm thinking: the user (like me) should be able to input basic info upfront — age, gender, weight maybe, whether they smoke or not — and then go through a series of questions about their symptoms. Not medical jargon, just plain language like "how often does your heart feel like it's racing" with options like "a few times a day / once or twice a week / rarely." I want it to cover stuff like dizziness, fatigue, chest tightness, sleep issues, headaches. Let people pick symptom frequency and how long it's been happening.

After they finish, show a clear risk level result — like a colored badge or something that's really obvious, maybe green/yellow/orange/red — and under it give a specific action recommendation, not just "consult a doctor" but something more like "your symptoms suggest you should see someone within 3 days" or "likely stress-related, try rest and hydration first." The result page should also show a short summary of what might be going on in plain language.

Design should be dark background with bright high-contrast text for the result section especially — I want the risk level to basically jump out at you. Should work well on mobile since people will mostly use this on their phone late at night. Add some kind of progress indicator while going through the questions so it doesn't feel endless. Maybe a small disclaimer at the bottom that this isn't a real diagnosis, just to be safe.

query_text:
Ok so I really need help building this outpatient appointment management app, specifically for people like me who have chronic stuff and keep seeing the same doctor over and over. I've got a back condition and I go back to my orthopedic doctor like every month or so, and the problem is I've already missed my queue twice because there was no proper reminder, and every single time I rebook I have to dig through the whole hospital search again just to find the same doctor — it's exhausting.

So here's what I'm thinking. The main page should be like a dashboard that shows everything in one shot — all my upcoming appointments, past records, and real-time queue status for today (like how many people are ahead of me). Reminders should be layered, not just one ping — maybe one when I should leave, one when I'm like 10 spots away from my turn. Just like how Didi shows you exactly where your driver is, that kind of live status feedback.

There should also be a "my doctors" section pinned near the top — a shortlist of doctors I've visited before so I can tap straight to my usual orthopedic doctor and see his open slots without any searching. Slots should be color-coded: green means open, orange means filling up, red means full.

Each appointment card needs a clear status badge — confirmed, waiting, completed, cancelled — and the whole design should feel bright and lively, saturated colors, nothing like the sad gray hospital interfaces I'm used to. Definitely mobile-first since I'm always doing this on my phone during lunch or my commute.
